sovereign_country.strategic_role: 北美成熟市场、联邦与省两级公司实体设立（EPC合规）

business_scope.primary_industry_name: C-Suite Executive Search and Specialist Tech Headhunting

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Canada–European Union Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA), provisionally in force
Canada–United States Tax Convention (1980, as amended)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, S.C. 2000, c. 17 (PCMLTFA) and Regulations (SOR/2002-184); Criminal Code (Canada) money laundering and terrorist financing provisions; Alberta Business Corporations Act, RSA 2000, c B-9, as amended, including ss. 114.1 and 124.1 respecting records and registers of individuals with significant control; Alberta Corporate Registry beneficial ownership reporting directives; United Nations Act, S.C. 1991, c. 45; Special Economic Measures Act, S.C. 1992, c. 17; Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act (Sergei Magnitsky Law), S.C. 2017, c. 23; FINTRAC reporting guidance and associated provincial privacy and corporate compliance decrees.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized copy of passport for each director, shareholder, and individual with significant control
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in country of residence / passport issuing authority
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Canada acceded effective January 11, 2024) or Consular Legalization if originating state is not an apostille party

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized proof of residential address (utility bill, bank statement, or government-issued certificate)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider / regulated financial institution / public registry in country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified extract of criminal/civil records or police clearance certificate for each proposed director and UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent police authority or judicial records office in country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and source-of-funds/wealth confirmation letter from principal remitting financial institution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Remitting bank or credit institution where retainer and wiring accounts are held
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Original bank letter authenticated by notary, then Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Pre-drafted Articles of Incorporation and Notice of Directors
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Applicant directors and incorporator preparatory legal counsel
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: To be notarized and submitted to Alberta Corporate Registry; apostille not required for domestic origin documents

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-incorporation KYC/CDD screening against the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN and non-SDN lists, Global Affairs Canada sanctions list under the Special Economic Measures Act, and the Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act list. All directors, officers, authorized signatories, shareholders, and beneficial owners must be identified and verified. Enhanced due diligence is required for any foreign or domestic politically exposed person (PEP) or individual with close associates/family members who are PEPs; such determinations require written senior-management approval, source-of-funds documentation, and a FATF-aligned risk assessment. Screening results and UBO records must be maintained internally for government inspection for at least five years and contemporaneously produced to FINTRAC or Alberta Corporate Registry upon demand.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Alberta Corporate Registry (Service Alberta) — official online portal and authorized service-provider network using the Corporate Registry System; name search conducted through the NUANS (Newly Upgraded Automated Name Search) system.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must be in English and/or French; where a non-Latin script is proposed, a romanized transliteration is required for registration and NUANS searching. The corporate ending (e.g., 'Inc.', 'Corp.', 'Ltd.', 'Incorporée' or 'Limitée') must appear as an integral part of the name, and the name must be distinctive, not merely descriptive, and not confusing with any existing corporate, trade type, or registered trademark. Disregarded terms, punctuation, and conjunctive words are acceptable only when they do not spoil distinctiveness.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon filing a NUANS report and prescribed application, the Director of Alberta Corporate Registry reserves the name for 90 days. A reservation may not be extended as a matter of right; the applicant may submit a new NUANS report and fresh reservation request before expiry to preserve priority. If the proposed name is rejected, the applicant receives a written statement of non-distinctiveness or confusion grounds. The applicant may file, within 30 days of rejection, a formal administrative appeal addressed to the Director of Corporate Registry, attaching the NUANS report, prior art and trademark consent letters, evidence of use or acquired distinctiveness, and any additional explanatory facts. A licensed Alberta legal counsel may represent the applicant at the administrative review stage; if the Director confirms rejection, the applicant may request judicial review before the Court of King's Bench of Alberta.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible for an executive search and headhunting agency. Alberta requires a registered office with a physical street address in Alberta at which notices and legal proceedings may be served during normal business hours. A virtual office or commercial registered-agent office is accepted provided that the registered office location is not a P.O. Box and documents are promptly forwarded to the company's actual management address. The industry does not mandate dedicated employment or meeting premises, but a substantive administrative, billing, and compliance presence must be maintained through the registered office, bookkeeping records, and transactional files.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low but real: approximately 10% probability of unannounced inspection within the first 18 months, driven mainly by FINTRAC AML supervision, financial payment-rail audits, and Alberta Corporate Registry compliance checks on annual return filings and UBO register accuracy. For a standard, low-risk executive headhunting entity, unannounced physical inspection is rare unless a regulatory complaint or AML red flag is reported.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff published by Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada and Alberta Registry fees; market benchmark approximately CAD 50.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Alberta Articles of Incorporation filing fee
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff under the Alberta Business Corporations Act and corporate registry fee schedule.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office and virtual commercial address for 12 months
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Alberta-licensed registered-office services provider / corporate agent
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for executive search industry (low-risk non-financial service).

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization and apostille bundle for international directors, shareholders, and UBO identification documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notary publics in relevant countries of origin; Global Affairs Canada Authentication and Apostille Services
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory notarial tariffs per certificate and prevailing authentication handling fees; variable by origination jurisdiction.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Beneficial ownership register, corporate minute book, and UBO compliance kit establishment
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Alberta-licensed corporate service provider / corporate lawyer
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for initial corporate records and Alberta Business Corporations Act register of individuals with significant control.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/CFT and PEP/sanctions screening policy preparation and internal compliance manual
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing professional hourly fee, approximate 3 to 4 hours of Canadian counsel at senior associate level; includes FINTRAC guidance alignment and SDN/UN screening framework incorporation.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Pre-filing legal opinion on corporate structure and non-resident ownership permissibility
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Alberta-qualified business or corporate transactional counsel
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for a written legal opinion under the Alberta Business Corporations Act on the proposed executive headhunting scope.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Alberta Business Corporations Act, RSA 2000, c. B-9, including sections 5-13 concerning incorporation and articles, sections 19-20 concerning registered office and records office, sections 102-106 concerning directors and organizational matters, and applicable provisions governing shares, officers, records, and corporate filings.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Service Alberta and Red Tape Reduction, Alberta Corporate Registry, accessed through an authorized Alberta registry agent or the applicable Alberta online corporate filing service.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation under the Alberta Business Corporations Act, together with the prescribed Corporate Registry application and registered-office information.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum issued or paid-up capital applies to an Alberta corporation. Shares may be issued for consideration authorized by the directors, subject to the articles, the Business Corporations Act, and stated corporate records. Alberta does not require a statutory incorporation escrow account. Any bank account used for subscription proceeds is a private banking arrangement, not a registry condition.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED THAT the Corporation accept and record the subscriptions for the shares specified in the incorporation documents and issue those shares as fully paid for the consideration received or legally payable. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT the registered office and records office stated in the Articles of Incorporation are adopted as the Corporation’s official offices until changed in accordance with law. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT [Name] is appointed President, [Name] Secretary, and [Name] Treasurer, each to serve at the pleasure of the directors. Any director or officer is authorized to complete filings, open bank accounts, execute contracts, and take all actions necessary to implement these resolutions.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Confirm Corporate Name and Incorporation Route
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry through an authorized Alberta registry agent; NUANS name-search services where a word name is proposed.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Select a numbered corporation or conduct a NUANS name search for a proposed distinctive name. Confirm that the name is not confusingly similar to an existing Alberta or federal entity and that the proposed activities are accurately described as executive recruitment, search, and placement services. Obtain written consent for any restricted or professional designation.
required_dossiers: Proposed corporate name or numbered-company request
NUANS report if required for the selected name
Written name-consent documents for restricted terms, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected, submit an amended name, a new NUANS report where required, or incorporate under a numbered name and later file a permissible name change.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry filing package prepared for submission through a registry agent or approved electronic channel.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Articles of Incorporation, registered office, records office, share structure, restrictions on share transfers, number of directors, and incorporator information. Ensure the articles do not authorize activities requiring a special statutory charter unless the relevant authorization has been obtained. Use an Alberta physical registered office and records-office address; a post-office box alone is insufficient.
required_dossiers: NUANS report or name reservation evidence, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct rejected or incomplete articles through the registry agent, replace defective addresses or share provisions, and resubmit with the registry query reference.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File Incorporation and Pay Registry Charges
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry, normally through an authorized registry agent.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the prescribed incorporation application, articles, name evidence, and identification materials. Pay the prescribed Alberta fee in Canadian dollars and obtain the certificate of incorporation, articles, corporate access number, and filed corporate documents. The stated USD amount is only a currency conversion estimate; Alberta charges in Canadian dollars and does not publish a USD filing fee.
required_dossiers: Signed or electronically authorized incorporation application
Registry-agent authorization, if filed by an agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to a registry deficiency notice through the filing agent, correct the prescribed form, and obtain confirmation that the resubmission has replaced the defective filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Complete Organizational Governance and Share Issuance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporation’s board of directors and internal corporate records office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the first directors’ meeting or execute written directors’ resolutions. Adopt the registered office, appoint officers, approve the banking mandate, approve the financial year-end, issue shares against documented consideration, authorize the securities register, and record beneficial ownership and control information required by applicable law. Do not backdate share issuances or director appointments.
required_dossiers: First board resolution or directors’ consent
Proof of consideration or subscription payment
Securities register and share certificates, if used
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Pass correcting resolutions, amend registers prospectively, document the original error, and obtain corporate legal review before filing any required correction or amendment.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register Tax, Payroll, and Provincial Accounts
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency, Alberta Tax and Revenue Administration where applicable, and the relevant municipal licensing office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain the CRA business number and register applicable GST/HST, payroll, and corporate income-tax program accounts. Register for workers’ compensation coverage if the business has covered Alberta workers. Confirm municipal business-licence requirements for the registered operating location and any home-office or client-site activities.
required_dossiers: Workers’ compensation registration materials, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct account classifications, provide additional CRA or municipal evidence, and request written confirmation of registration or exemption.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Conditional Employment-Agency and Operational Approvals
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Service Alberta and Red Tape Reduction, Consumer Investigations and Licensing; the applicable Alberta municipality; and Alberta Employment Standards where employment-placement rules apply.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Determine whether the operating model constitutes an employment-agency business, recruitment of foreign nationals, temporary-help services, or only executive-search advisory services. Apply for any required provincial or municipal employment-agency or business licence before commencing regulated placement activity. Adopt written rules prohibiting unlawful worker-paid recruitment fees and maintain client, candidate, consent, and placement records.
required_dossiers: Foreign-worker recruitment compliance assessment, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to licensing queries, narrow the activity description, provide missing ownership or premises information, request a written exemption determination, or appeal or seek review under the applicable licensing statute.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Service Alberta and Red Tape Reduction, Consumer Investigations and Licensing, together with the applicable municipal business-licensing authority. A standard executive-search office is not subject to a general provincial manufacturing licence; licensing is activity- and municipality-dependent.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Employment Agency or Recruitment Business Licence, where required by the applicable Alberta regulatory regime or municipality; otherwise, the applicable municipal business licence for an executive-search office.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Generally exempt or not applicable for a conventional office-based executive-search and recruitment business with no industrial process, significant emissions, wastewater system, or hazardous-waste operation. A site-specific review is required if the business operates a facility or activity falling within Alberta environmental approval requirements.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No routine industrial discharge or VOC threshold normally applies to an office-based search firm. The operator must comply with applicable municipal wastewater bylaws, Alberta Environmental Protection and Enhancement Act approvals, federal hazardous-products and waste rules, and approved waste-hauler requirements. Any hazardous, biomedical, solvent, fuel, or electronic waste must be segregated, documented, and transferred to an authorized handler.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Obtain municipal occupancy and business-premises approval where required, maintain fire alarms, emergency exits, extinguishers, evacuation procedures, and accessible egress in accordance with the Alberta Fire Code and the local authority having jurisdiction. Structural-load inspection is required only where premises alterations, storage loads, mezzanines, or building-code triggers apply. Comply with Alberta Occupational Health and Safety legislation, including hazard assessment, violence prevention, ergonomics, incident reporting, and worker training requirements. No industrial occupational clearance is ordinarily required for ordinary office-based executive search.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada (ARC), GST/HST Program Directorate, administered through the Business Registration Online (BRO) portal and the CRA My Business Account platform (https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency.html)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A non-resident entity incorporates under the Canada Business Corporations Act (CBCA) or Alberta Business Corporations Act via the Alberta Corporate Registry; concurrent registration for the 9-digit Business Number (BN), corporate income tax account, and GST/HST account is completed through CRA Business Registration Online (BRO) using Form RC1 (Request for Business Number); the entity must appoint counsel-for-service in Canada, provide certified copy of articles of incorporation, Alberta extra-provincial registration certificate (if federal incorporation), director/officer residency particulars, and a Canadian administrative contact; CRA issues a single BN with a separate 2-digit RT (corporate tax) and 2-digit RM (GST/HST) program account; GST/HST registration is mandatory immediately if the aggregate worldwide taxable supplies exceed the CAD 30,000 small-supplier threshold.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation (resident corporation taxed on worldwide income under ITA ss. 2, 3, 9; Alberta branch of foreign corporation taxed under Part I plus Part I.3 surtax and Part XIV branch tax; non-Canadian-controlled corporation is not an SPC or QSBC, therefore disqualified from the Small Business Deduction; Alberta general corporate rate is 8% plus federal 15% for a combined statutory rate of approximately 23%), with territorial scope: worldwide income taxation for Canadian resident corporations and Canada-source business income taxation for non-resident corporations; province of Alberta does not levy a separate capital tax or provincial sales tax, making Alberta a Provincial Sales Tax (PST) exempt zone.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada does not employ a US-style check-the-box regime; relevant elections include: ITA s. 216(1) election (net-basis taxation of Canadian rental income), ITA s. 217 election (net-basis taxation of certain pension income), ITA s. 115 tax treaty protection declaration, Part XIV branch tax reduction election for treaty-protected surplus, ETA s. 156 joint election for closely related corporations (supplies deemed made for nil consideration), ETA s. 179 election for selected financial institutions, and GST/HST s. 225.2 substantive office joint election; hybrid mismatch rules apply through GAAR and specific anti-hybrid provisions, plus CRA Form RC4648 technical interpretation requests.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax (GST) under Part IX of the Excise Tax Act, Canada; Harmonized Sales Tax (HST) applies only in participating provinces (Ontario, Nova Scotia, New Brunswick, PEI, Newfoundland and Labrador, plus partial in BC for PST only); Alberta imposes no provincial sales tax.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 aggregate worldwide gross taxable supplies (excluding zero-rated export supplies) in any single calendar quarter or over the trailing four consecutive calendar quarters; non-residents carrying on business in Canada must register regardless of threshold if making taxable supplies in Canada; threshold for listed financial institutions and certain supply-members of partnerships differs; once exceeded, mandatory registration within one month of exceeding.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandatory real-time fiscal clearance, government-validated digital stamping, or continuous transaction control framework exists in Canada; CRA does not require API-based pre-clearance of invoices; taxpayers are obligated under ETA s. 286 to retain electronic books and records in an accessible machine-readable format; GST/HST returns must be filed electronically (GST/HST NETFILE) when gross revenue exceeds CAD 1.5 million, otherwise paper or NETFILE; CRA has adopted the Pan-Canadian Peppol interoperability framework for voluntary B2B e-invoicing, with no statutory issuance mandate; invoices must contain prescribed information including supplier BN, GST/HST registration number, tax charged, supplier name, and transaction date.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under ETA Schedule VI, Part V, section 7, advisory, professional, consulting, and similar services (including executive search and headhunting services) are zero-rated when supplied to a non-resident person, provided (i) the recipient is not registered for GST/HST, (ii) the recipient is not an individual physically present in Canada at the time the service is performed, and (iii) the service is not in connection with real property situated in Canada or tangible personal property situated in Canada at the time the service is performed; zero-rating also applies to services of a headhunter performed entirely offshore for a foreign employer, including candidate sourcing, retained search, reference verification, and interim executive placement, where the benefit of the service is received outside Canada; supporting evidence must establish the non-resident status of the client (foreign registration certificate, foreign tax residency certificate, foreign address) and the offshore delivery or use of the service.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Canada Customs Export Declaration (B13A) filed via Canadian Export Declaration System (CAED) or CBSA portal where physical deliverables, onboarding kits, or market research documents are shipped cross-border
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing physical export of any goods related to the engagement
Inward Remittance Certificate and SWIFT/MT103 wire confirmation evidencing foreign-currency remittance from the non-resident client
Executed executive search retainer agreement and engagement letter demonstrating the non-resident scope, offshore delivery, and foreign payment obligations
Non-resident client proof of residence (foreign corporate registry extract, tax identification number, certificate of residence)
Candidate placement and service delivery records proving all substantive headhunting services were performed outside Canada
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA reassessment window is 4 years for ordinary matters and 10 years in cases of misrepresentation, fraud, or omission under ETA s. 298; a wholly unsupported zero-rating claim triggers full reversal of the zero rating, resultant GST/HST liability, interest compounded daily under ETA s. 280, and reduction of input tax credits; gross negligence penalty of 50% of the net tax understated applies under ETA s. 285(1) (mirroring ITA s. 163(2)); false statements carry penalties up to CAD 25,000 on summary conviction; indictable conviction for evasion under ETA s. 327(1) attracts fines up to 200% of the amount sought to be evaded and imprisonment for up to 5 years; clawback interest accrues from the original filing date; directors and officers remain jointly and severally liable for unremitted GST/HST up to withholding obligations; CRA jurisdictional audit program specifically flags headhunting firms claiming zero-rating on services to US and Hong Kong clients where no separate export documentation bundle or remittance proof is retained.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full market convertibility with no substantive capital controls; current-account and capital-account transactions are freely convertible. Profit remittance hurdles primarily consist of corporate solvency tests under Alberta Business Corporations Act and domestic withholding tax on dividends paid to non-residents (standard 25%, potentially treaty-reduced). No foreign-exchange licensing or prior central bank approval is required for cross-border remittances.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory export surrender obligation in Canada. Export receipts may be fully retained in foreign currency or converted at commercial Canadian-dollar exchange rates. There is no mandated conversion ratio or timeline.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Business Operating and Foreign Currency Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium for supplementary cross-border payment rails, but Low for primary treasury infrastructure. Canadian regulation does not license foreign EMIs as banks; they must register as Money Service Businesses (MSBs) with FINTRAC under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act. Wise B2B is an acceptable supplementary rail for small-value remittances, but cannot replace a Canadian-owned deposit account for clearing, settlement, or credit facilities.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical appearance of at least one director or authorized signatory is usually expected at account opening, but most Schedule I banks and credit unions now permit remote video identification if corporate documentation is certified. For a federally or Alberta-registered corporation, a remote opening with a digital notarized corporate package is viable for the target entity. Institutions may still require a local business mailing address and proof of operational substance in Canada.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership chain involving non-resident or offshore shareholders; financial institution risk-rating may escalate to high.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified corporate register (up-to-date register of directors and shareholders), Alberta or federal extraprovincial registration certificate, tax confirmation for UBO identity, source-of-funds declaration, audited financial statements or pro-forma statements, and board resolution approving the banking mandate.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mismatch between stated commercial model (headhunting) and payment flows to/from third-party professional service providers, causing plausibility risk.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Standard form client agreements, retainer invoices, candidate placement contracts, professional liability insurance certificate, detailed narrative of fee-flow, and banking references from previous financial institution.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Receipt of cross-border wires from jurisdictions with heightened AML/CFT scrutiny; no evident business relationship.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Business intelligence report on ultimate client entity, client KYB documentation (certificate of incorporation, registry extracts, UBO list), commercial rationale memo, and compliance due diligence evidence from reputable sanctions and PEP screening.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Use SWIFT MT103 (ISO 20022 camt/pa.002 for reconciliation) from the remitting shareholder. Remitter legal entity name must match the shareholder record, and reference must include 'Share subscription – [Corporate Name]' to classify the capital injection. The receiving institution will apply FINTRAC large-value transaction reporting at CAD 10,000 for incoming wires and may request a statement of source of funds. Purpose code in Canada is bank-internal; use 'Equity Injection' or 'Investment in Canadian Business' and identify the jurisdiction of origin.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For service payments to foreign consultants and contractors, use SWIFT MT103 with supporting invoice and service agreement. Commercial Letters of Credit (LC) are not typical for professional services; instead use electronic fund transfers or, for covered trade, SWIFT MT700 LC when goods are involved. Use 'Trade settlement under contract EXEC-SRCH-' reference to match underlying agreement; the clearing rails are CDN payment system (ACSS/Lynx for CAD, USCH for USD) and SWIFT for cross-border.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forwards (up to 24 months) against CAD/USD/EUR/GBP

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Alberta Annual Return – Corporation (annual corporate registry filing for an ABCA-incorporated entity)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry (Service Alberta) via licensed registry agent
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days (2 calendar months) after the anniversary of incorporation or of the last annual return; anniversary-based, not tied to fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No monetary late fee; failure to file for two consecutive years permits the Registrar to administratively dissolve the corporation; revival available on application within 5 years with payment of arrears and fees.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: CBCA Annual Return (mandatory only for a Canada Business Corporations Act federal incorporation)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporations Canada, Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada (ISED)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the anniversary of the date of incorporation or of the last recognized CBCA annual return date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No statutory late surcharge; after a notice of default and continued non-compliance beyond 120 days, the Director of Corporations may administratively dissolve the corporation under CBCA s. 211.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Alberta Annual Return – Extra-Provincial Corporation (required only where a CBCA or out-of-province corporation is registered to carry on business in Alberta)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the anniversary of the extra-provincial registration date or of the last annual return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Registration certificate may be cancelled after two consecutive missed annual returns; the corporation then has no legal authority to carry on business in Alberta until revived.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal T2 Corporation Income Tax Return (federal and Alberta corporate income tax assessed through a single CRA filing)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Six months after fiscal year-end; for a December 31 fiscal year-end, the return is due by June 30 of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty under ITA s. 162(1): 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per full month of delay, to a maximum of 12 months; repeat failure doubles the penalty (10% plus 2%, maximum 24 months); daily compound interest runs on arrears; gross negligence penalty up to 50% of tax avoided; continued non-filing may trigger arbitrary assessment and prosecution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T4 Statement of Remuneration and T4 Summary (annual payroll reconciliation)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before the last business day of February following the calendar year to which the remuneration relates
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Information-return penalties under ITA s. 162(7) scale by number of T4 slips (CAD 100 to CAD 2,500); additional daily penalties of CAD 25 per return may apply after a CRA demand; late distribution of employee copies is separately penalized.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 23% (15% federal general corporate rate + 8% Alberta general corporate rate)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Federal SR&ED investment tax credit up to 35% for qualifying Canadian-controlled private corporations; Alberta Innovation Employment Grant up to 20% of eligible payroll growth; no preferential headline rate for executive-search/headhunting activities

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return filed via CRA EFILE / e-File portal; Alberta corporate income tax is integrated within the T2 through provincial schedule (Schedule 5 – Alberta)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual return; quarterly instalments required where corporate tax payable exceeds CAD 3,000
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: T2 return due no later than 6 months after fiscal year-end; balance-due date is 2 months after year-end for non-CCPCs (3 months for CCPCs)

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net income (loss) for income tax purposes before loss carryovers, reconciled from financial statements; adjust for non-deductible and non-taxable items
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident taxpayers file only if carrying on business through a Canadian permanent establishment; report Alberta business income derived from fee-based headhunting services; exclude all foreign-source unrelated income

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after deducting non-capital loss carryovers, eligible treaty deductions, and prior-year adjustments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply Canada-Alberta statutory filing principles; claim treaty-dependent deductions only to the extent they are connected with the Canadian permanent establishment; substantiate with contemporaneous records

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Alberta taxable income and provincial tax calculation using the Alberta 8% rate; requires allocation of federal taxable income under Alberta allocation rules
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Allocate income using the Alberta GRID-based apportionment factors if the non-resident has a permanent establishment in Alberta; omit if no Alberta permanent establishment

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disclosure forms for non-arm's-length cross-border transactions, non-resident payments, and provincial allocation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach T106 where aggregate cross-border non-arm's-length transactions exceed CAD 1,000,000; report Part XIII withholding in NR4 for fees remitted to foreign headhunting affiliates or overseas subcontractors

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late-filing penalty is 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per full month late, up to 12 months; repeated failure penalty is 10%; prescribed interest on arrears accrues daily

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% under Part XIII of the Income Tax Act for dividends paid to non-resident parent or shareholder unless reduced by an applicable tax treaty
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Before remittance, beneficial owner submits Form NR301 (or NR302 where applicable) to the Canadian withholding agent or CRA, together with a valid foreign tax residence certificate; documentation must establish treaty residence, beneficial ownership, and ownership thresholds; CRA may approve a treaty-based withholding reduction before payment, and the payer reports the reduced amount on forms NR4/ T106
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory Part XIII rate is 25% on IP royalties and debt interest; under Canada's DTAs rates are typically reduced to 15% for portfolio interest/royalties and to 5–10% for direct-investment dividends; under the Canada-China DTA, interest and royalties are generally reduced to 10% with a 10% direct-investment dividend rate

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: T106 filing is mandatory for taxpayers with aggregate reportable non-arm's-length cross-border transactions exceeding CAD 1,000,000; CRA expects contemporaneous Transfer Pricing documentation below this threshold, and Master File/Local File requirements crystallize for MNE groups with consolidated annual gross revenue of CAD 1,000,000,000 or more
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada does not operate a discrete Economic Substance Regulations regime; however, the CRA applies legal and economic substance analysis through permanent establishment principles, the General Anti-Avoidance Rule (ITA s.245), and transfer-pricing recharacterization; a headhunting entity that is a mere booking office without employees, office infrastructure, and real decision-making is treated as lacking substance and may have its fee flows recharacterized as taxable Canadian business income or deemed dividends

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intentionally omitting Canadian-source executive-search retainers from a T2 return, issuing backdated invoices, or using offshore shell accounts to conceal fees earned by a Canadian corporation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under ITA s.238/s.239, conviction carries a fine up to 200% of the tax evaded and imprisonment for up to 5 years; CRA imposes gross negligence penalties of 50% of understated tax plus interest
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be jointly and severally liable for amounts evaded under the Income Tax Act; CRA may seek civil restitution, register certificates against personal assets, and request passport denial/revocation for tax debts above CAD 500 where payment arrangements are absent

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Incorporating a Canadian header/booking entity with no employees, no office, no board minutes, and routing all actual headhunting activity through a low-tax foreign affiliate while booking commissioning income in Canada without local economic substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: CRA recharacterizes the fee flows under GAAR or transfer-pricing rules, applies the full Part XIII 25% withholding on deemed dividends, disallows deductions, and imposes gross negligence penalties; no specific monetary cap for GAAR adjustments
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be held personally liable for Part XIII withholding and unremitted source deductions through director liability certificates; criminal exposure under conspiracy or fraud provisions may add imprisonment and travel restrictions

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Charging a foreign related party an inflated commission, management fee, or service fee to erode Canadian taxable income without an arm's-length comparability analysis; failing to prepare and retain Local File/Master File documentation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: ITA s.247(3) imposes a transfer-pricing penalty equal to 10% of the net transfer-pricing adjustment; interest and gross negligence penalties may also apply; recharacterization of the intercompany fee can result in Part XIII withholding deemed dividends
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and senior officers who knowingly participated in or acquiesced to deficient transfer-pricing documentation can be assessed under joint liability provisions or under directors' liability for unremitted withholding; civil liability is not dischargeable in bankruptcy

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using Wise B2B or similar retainer rails to move funds in and out of Canada without FINTRAC registration, client identification records, transaction reporting, or filing a money-services-business remittance report where required
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act penalties up to CAD 500,000 for corporations and CAD 100,000 for individuals per violation; administrative monetary penalties and compliance orders apply
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Officers and directors who exercise direction over AML compliance may be found personally liable under FINTRAC amendments; senior managers face imprisonment for knowingly causing false reporting, and travel bans can be imposed as part of bail or court-ordered asset restraint

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Misclassifying executive-search recruiters as independent contractors to avoid CPP/EI, failing to remit Canada Pension Plan, Employment Insurance, and GST/HST, or acquiring general contractor status outside Alberta licensing requirements
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Failure to remit source deductions results in 10% penalty plus prescribed daily interest; GST/HST non-registration triggers 25% failure-to-register penalty on net tax; compliance orders may freeze business bank accounts
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally liable under ITA s.227.1 and ETA s.323 for unremitted employer withholdings and GST/HST, regardless of corporate dissolution; CRA may pursue seizures of personal property, passport denials, and legal proceedings for fraud-related offenses
